sections.title: Card choice splits two ways
sections.sub: Crypto cards are designed for two different purposes. RedotPay, OKX Card and Ether.fi Cash are cashback-focused cards built around payment rewards. Anytap Card is a function-focused card built around limits and money mobility. The two cannot be optimal at the same time.

sections.label: GLOBAL TREND
p: Across the global crypto card market, users worn down by the cashback race are moving to function-focused cards. Repeated rate cuts, newly introduced accrual caps, tightened staking requirements and suspended referral commissions have made clear that whoever picks a card for its rewards is the one carrying the risk of the terms changing.

As a result, a growing share of users choose on a different test: is the limit sufficient, can funds move as needed, and can the total cost be calculated in advance? That is why Crypto Cards Info separates the two card types explicitly.

The best card is not the one with the highest cashback. We set out the order in which to check.
Twenty plain-language answers on stablecoins, top-ups, FX spread, KYC, ATM fees and more.

sections.title: Compare the real total cost
p: Advertised numbers usually describe a single line item. What a user actually bears is the issuance fee, the top-up fee, the crypto conversion fee, the FX fee and spread, the foreign payment fee and ATM costs, added together and then reduced by the cashback actually received.
CryptoCardsInfo therefore compares the final total cost of using a card rather than the lowest headline rate.

sections.label: EDITORIAL PRINCIPLES
p: All information is presented objectively; no card or company is unconditionally recommended or criticised.

Official websites, terms, fee schedules and notices are used as primary sources. Where a figure cannot be verified, we do not estimate — we mark it 'Check official source' or 'Not disclosed officially'.
Marketing phrases such as '0% fees' or 'up to X% cashback' are always shown separately from the conditions that actually apply. The final choice rests with the user.

fee-comparison.desc: Compare crypto card issuance fees, top-up fees, crypto conversion costs, FX spread, foreign payment fees and ATM costs.
fee-comparison.lead: '0% fees' does not mean the real cost is zero. Costs can arise at every stage that money moves — top-up, crypto conversion, FX and spread, payment, foreign payment and ATM withdrawal.

sections.title: Where does the real cost arise?
sections.sub: Rather than the headline 0%, check how much finally leaves your pocket.

steps.d: A top-up fee may apply when loading the card balance.
The cost of converting holdings into a spendable asset.
The applied rate and its spread (markup) change what you actually pay.
Check the settlement currency and how the rate is handled at the moment of payment.
Network-standard fees may apply at overseas merchants.
Cash withdrawals may carry their own rate and minimum charge.
Issuance + top-up + conversion + FX + spread + foreign payment + ATM − cashback actually received

sections.label: REAL TOTAL COST
p: The purpose of comparison is not to find the lowest headline rate but to see what you finally bear in real use.
Real total cost = issuance fee + top-up fee + crypto conversion fee + FX fee + FX spread + foreign payment fee + ATM cost − cashback actually received.
Even for the same amount spent, the total cost differs with the top-up route and the payment currency.

sections.label: CONSUMER WARNING
sections.big: A provider that does not publish its fees transparently on its official site cannot be treated as trustworthy.
p: Publishing a fee schedule is not a matter of provider discretion; it belongs to the basic duty to let users understand the contract terms in advance. If issuance, top-up, conversion, FX spread, foreign payment and ATM charges cannot each be verified on the official site or in the official terms, the user cannot calculate the total cost before entering into the contract.

Where a provider offers only phrases such as 'free', '0% fees' or 'the lowest in the industry' without stating rates, the possibility cannot be excluded that the real cost is embedded in the FX spread or the conversion step and never displayed. It is rational to rank a provider whose marketing copy does not match its official fee schedule lower in any comparison.

CryptoCardsInfo does not estimate figures where the following three items cannot be verified, and marks them 'Check official source': an official fee schedule stating each rate; a stated procedure for advance notice of rate changes; and the basis of the applied exchange rate, including whether it is the card network reference rate and the size of any markup.

Before choosing a card, confirm whether a fee schedule is published on the official site or in the terms, whether the history and method of notice for rate changes can be verified, and whether you can calculate the total cost yourself without contacting support. If any of these cannot be confirmed, test with a small payment and verify the actual charge before depositing funds.

sections.label: IMPORTANT NOTICE FOR USERS
sections.big: A provider that does not publish its fees transparently on its official site cannot be an object of trust.
p: Publishing a fee schedule is not a matter of provider discretion; it belongs to the basic duty to disclose information so that users can know the terms of the contract in advance. If the issuance fee, top-up fee, conversion fee, FX spread, foreign payment fee and ATM fee cannot be verified line by line on the official site or in the official terms, the user simply cannot calculate the total cost before contracting.

Where a provider offers only expressions such as 'free', '0% fees' or 'lowest in the industry' without stating rates, the possibility that the real cost is embedded in the FX spread or the conversion step — and therefore not displayed — cannot be excluded. It is reasonable to rank providers whose marketing copy does not match their official fee schedule lower in any comparison.

sections.title: Why the headline rate and the amount received differ

items.d: Cashback is proportional to spend. At 3%, spending USD 400 in a month accrues about USD 12.
With a cap in place, spending more does not increase what you receive beyond that ceiling.
Where a higher rate depends on staking the issuer's own token, the price risk and opportunity cost of the locked assets fall on the user.
If cashback is paid in a proprietary token or points, the real value can change even when the rate does not.
Rates, caps and payout methods can be varied or suspended under the terms.
Top-ups, transfers, certain categories and cash-like transactions are often excluded from accrual.

sections.label: THE MOST IMPORTANT CHECK
sections.big: If the fee schedule is not published, the saving cannot be calculated.
p: The cashback rate is the last item to check. What comes first is whether an itemised fee schedule is published, the basis of the applied exchange rate and the size of the markup, and the procedure for advance notice of rate changes. Without those three in official material, no advertised cashback rate allows you to compute the real saving.

Whether the card balance can be returned to an external wallet is also directly tied to provider risk. If there is no route back out after funds are deposited, your options are limited when policy changes or a service is discontinued.

sections.label: THE DECISION IS YOURS
p: CryptoCardsInfo sets out comparison criteria and items to check; it does not rank any card first.
The final choice, made after checking official material, rests with the user.

faq.title: Crypto Card FAQ | Beginner's Guide to Crypto Cards | CryptoCardsInfo
faq.desc: Plain explanations of crypto debit cards, stablecoins, top-ups, FX spread, fees, cashback, KYC and other basic terms.
faq.lead: Basic concepts and terminology for people using a crypto card for the first time. These are general explanations; actual terms must be confirmed in the official material of the service you intend to use.

items: What is a crypto debit card?
A prepaid or debit card that lets you spend crypto assets or stablecoins you hold. Typically you load assets into a card account and then pay at merchants on a network such as Visa.
Am I paying merchants directly in crypto?

In most cases the crypto is converted into fiat at the moment of payment and the merchant is paid in fiat. The merchant processes it like any card payment while the asset is deducted from your account.
What is a stablecoin?

A crypto asset designed to track the value of a reference asset such as the US dollar. Price movement is relatively small, which is why it is widely used for payments, though issuer reserve and credit risk remain.
How do USDT and USDC differ?
Both track the US dollar but differ in issuer, reserve disclosure practice, supported networks and which services accept them. Check which asset and network your card supports before topping up.
What is a top-up?
Loading the balance you can spend with the card. It is usually done by sending assets from a personal wallet or an exchange, and a top-up fee may apply at this stage.
Does a currency conversion happen when I pay?
If the payment currency differs from the currency of your card balance, a conversion occurs. The rate applied and any additional fee determine what you actually pay.
What are the exchange rate and spread?
Spread is the difference between the reference rate and the rate actually applied. Even at a stated 0% fee, a wide spread increases the real cost.
What kinds of card fees exist?
Issuance fee, annual fee, top-up fee, crypto conversion fee, FX fee and spread, foreign payment fee and ATM fee. Only by separating them can you see the total cost.
How is cashback calculated?
Usually the rate is applied to qualifying spend, then the monthly cap and excluded transactions are applied. The payout asset and its usage terms also affect real value.
Is a higher cashback rate always better?
No. Once accrual caps, staking requirements, the value of the payout asset and top-up or FX fees are included, real savings can look very different.
What is fiat?
Government-issued legal tender, such as the Korean won, the US dollar or the euro.
What is a stablecoin, in short?
A crypto asset designed to follow the value of a reference asset such as a fiat currency; it is frequently used for payment and settlement.
What is a wallet?
Software or hardware for holding and sending crypto assets. It may be self-custodial, where you hold the private key, or custodial, where a provider holds it.
What is a blockchain network?
The network on which transactions are recorded and transmitted. The same asset on a different network follows a different route and carries different fees.
What is a gas or network fee?
The fee paid to the blockchain network to process a transaction. It arises separately from the card provider's fees.
What are on-ramp and off-ramp?
On-ramp is the route from fiat into crypto; off-ramp is the route from crypto back into fiat.
What is KYC?
The process by which a financial service provider verifies a user's identity. It is often required for card issuance and higher limits.
What is an FX fee?
A foreign currency fee charged when the payment currency differs from the card's settlement currency. Both network and provider rates may apply.
What is an ATM fee?
The fee a card provider charges for a cash withdrawal at an ATM, often expressed as a rate together with a minimum amount.
What is a card-to-card transfer?
A feature that moves a card balance directly between users of the same service. Availability, fees and limits differ by service.

privacy.lead: CryptoCardsInfo operates as an information service and does not require sign-up or the entry of personal data to use the site.

p: This site offers no sign-up, login or payment function and does not directly collect identifying information such as names, contact details or account numbers.

For operation and security, technical information such as access logs, browser type and access time may be generated and recorded automatically. Such information is used only for statistical analysis and fault response.
Browser storage may be used for convenience features such as language preference. Users may refuse storage through browser settings, in which case some convenience features may be limited.

items.t: Article 4 (Disclosure and processing on our behalf)
p: This site does not sell or provide users' personal data to third parties. Processing may, however, be entrusted to service providers to the extent necessary for operation, such as web hosting and analytics.
Where you move to an external service, that site's privacy practices apply. This site is not responsible for personal data handling on external sites.
Automatically generated information is retained only for the period necessary for operational and security purposes and is then destroyed.
Users may request access to, correction of, deletion of or suspension of processing of their information in accordance with applicable law.
This policy may be amended in line with changes in law or the composition of the service; the last-updated date on this page will change accordingly.

principles.title: Editorial Principles | CryptoCardsInfo
principles.desc: The editorial principles and verification standards applied across CryptoCardsInfo.
principles.lead: CryptoCardsInfo is not a site that sells crypto cards; it is a specialist information publication that helps users judge real costs and features for themselves. The following principles apply consistently across the site.

items.d: No card or company is unconditionally recommended or criticised. Strengths and limitations are given equal weight.
We provide comparison criteria and items to check; the final choice and decision to use a service rest with the user.
Official websites, terms, fee schedules, help centres, announcements and policy documents are used as primary sources.
We do not estimate. Unverified items are marked 'unable to verify', 'not disclosed officially', 'not currently verifiable' or 'check official source'.
Phrases such as '0% fees' or 'up to X% cashback' are shown separately from the conditions that actually apply.
Only genuinely changed information is updated; dates are never refreshed merely to make content look new.

sections.title: How verification is marked
p: Where a value cannot be confirmed in official material, we neither leave it blank nor estimate it: we mark it 'check official source' or 'not disclosed officially'. The marking does not mean the feature or condition is absent — it means the user must confirm it in official material.
Verification dates record only the day the material was actually checked and are never refreshed automatically.
